policy: Standard Croatian; retain distinct grammatical forms; correct misleading hints and keep notes concise.

je.note: Unstressed third-person singular of biti: he/she/it is. Also a past-tense auxiliary and a short form of 'her'.

da.note: Means 'yes' as an answer, or introduces a clause ('that'). Other uses depend on the construction.

se.note: Short reflexive pronoun, used with verbs such as prati se. It has no single English equivalent and does not mean 'are'.

u.note: With locative for location ('in'); with accusative for movement into somewhere. Also means 'at' in time expressions.

to.note: Neuter singular demonstrative, nominative/accusative. Can stand for 'that' or 'it'.

sam.note: Usually the short first-person singular of biti, also a past-tense auxiliary. As an adjective, sam means 'alone' (masculine).

ti.note: Informal singular subject 'you'; also the short dative pronoun 'to you'. Context distinguishes them.

mi.note: Either the subject pronoun 'we' or the short dative 'to me'. These are different pronouns with the same spelling.

li.note: Unstressed particle used in yes/no questions, usually after a verb: znaš li? It has no direct English translation.

ja.note: First-person singular subject pronoun. Often omitted because the verb already identifies the person.

su.note: Short third-person plural of biti: 'they are'; also used as a past-tense auxiliary.

nije.note: Negative third-person singular of biti. With a past participle, forms a negative past tense.

s.note: With instrumental means 'with'; with genitive can mean 'from/off'. Sa is a longer pronunciation variant.

ga.note: Short genitive/accusative pronoun for masculine or neuter singular: 'him/it', with the English wording set by context.

me.note: Short genitive/accusative of ja. The longer, stressed form is mene.

bi.note: Conditional auxiliary for ti, on/ona/ono and oni/one/ona; used with a past participle. First-person singular uses bih.

te.note: Short genitive/accusative of ti ('you'); also a conjunction meaning 'and'.

će.note: Short future auxiliary for third-person singular or plural: he/she/it/they will. Used with an infinitive.

o.note: With locative usually means 'about'; accusative occurs in expressions of contact or time, such as o zid and o Božić.

sa.note: Longer form of s, especially before s, z, š, ž and in sa mnom. Case determines 'with' versus 'from/off'.

sve.note: Often 'everything' (neuter singular); also several plural/case forms of sav. The noun and construction determine agreement.

ću.note: First-person singular future auxiliary. It can precede the infinitive or follow its shortened form: ću raditi / radit ću.

nisam.note: Negative first-person singular of biti. With a past participle it gives 'I did not/have not'; alone it means 'I am not'.

bio.note: Masculine singular past participle of biti. Usually combines with an auxiliary: bio sam ('I was').

mogu.note: Present of moći, first-person singular or third-person plural. Both forms have the same spelling.

redu.note: Dative/locative singular of red. The phrase u redu means 'all right' or 'OK'.

bilo.note: Neuter singular past participle of biti. Also appears in bilo tko ('anyone') and bilo…bilo ('either…or').

kad.note: Short form of kada ('when'); standard Croatian, not restricted to informal speech.

koji.note: Masculine singular interrogative/relative form. Unlike tko, it agrees with the noun it refers to.

vas.note: Genitive/accusative of plural or polite vi. The possessive 'your' is vaš, not vas.

ih.note: Short genitive/accusative plural pronoun ('them'); the stressed form is njih.

mu.note: Short dative pronoun: to him/to it. The full, stressed form is njemu.

ćemo.note: First-person plural future auxiliary ('we will'), used with an infinitive.

bila.note: Past participle of biti: feminine singular or neuter plural. An auxiliary identifies the person.

nas.note: Genitive/accusative of mi ('we'). The possessive 'our' is naš, not nas.

mene.note: Long, stressed genitive/accusative of ja. Used after prepositions, for contrast or emphasis; short form me.

kada.note: Means 'when'; kad is a standard shorter variant. Both are used in questions and time clauses.

prije.note: Can mean 'before' (with genitive), 'earlier', or 'ago' in a time expression.

tebe.note: Long, stressed genitive/accusative of ti. Used after prepositions or for emphasis; short form te.

hej.note: Interjection for greeting someone or attracting attention; informal.

imam.note: First-person singular present of imati. Also the spelling of the noun imam, an Islamic religious leader.

sad.note: Adverb meaning now. Uppercase SAD is also the abbreviation for the United States; matching here ignores case.

tu.note: Usually 'here/there at that place'; can also be a feminine accusative form of taj ('that').

ćeš.note: Second-person singular future auxiliary ('you will'), used with an infinitive.

nam.note: Short dative of mi ('we'). The stressed form is nama.

nisi.note: Negative second-person singular of biti. With a past participle it forms a negative past tense.

zato.note: Points to a consequence or reason already mentioned. Zato što, as a phrase, means 'because'.

baš.note: An emphatic particle meaning 'really', 'exactly' or 'just', depending on what it modifies.

bez.note: Preposition followed by genitive. The colour 'beige' is bež, a different word.

koje.note: Form of koji: commonly neuter singular or feminine plural; also feminine genitive singular and masculine accusative plural.

joj.note: Short dative of ona ('she'); also an interjection expressing pain, alarm or surprise.

toga.note: Genitive singular of taj/to; also masculine animate accusative. Can separately be the noun toga, a Roman garment.

žao.note: Used in žao mi je ('I am sorry/I regret it'). The English word 'evil' is not an appropriate hint here.

tome.note: Dative/locative masculine or neuter singular of taj/to. The ending does not identify the case without context.

mogao.note: Masculine singular past participle of moći ('can'). Used in past and conditional constructions with auxiliaries.

dana.note: Genitive singular or plural of dan ('day'); also a feminine form of the passive participle dan ('given').

moje.note: Form of moj ('my'): agrees with the possessed noun. Commonly neuter singular, feminine plural or feminine genitive singular.

put.note: Means an occasion ('prvi put'), way/journey/road, or 'towards' as a preposition. Context distinguishes these uses.

daj.note: Singular imperative of dati ('give'); also used conversationally to urge someone: 'come on'.

meni.note: Dative/locative of ja; a stressed form, often used after prepositions. Separately, meni can mean a restaurant menu.

kod.note: Preposition with genitive for location 'at/by/near'; also a masculine noun meaning 'code'.

jeste.note: Stressed second-person plural of biti, also used for polite singular address. Standard Croatian third-person singular is jest.

dva.note: Number 'two' with masculine or neuter nouns. Feminine nouns use dvije.

nismo.note: Negative first-person plural of biti; also a past-tense auxiliary when followed by a past participle.

niste.note: Negative second-person plural of biti, also polite singular. A following past participle makes it a negative past tense.

sebe.note: Stressed genitive/accusative reflexive pronoun. It can refer to any grammatical person, not only 'yourself'.

sebi.note: Dative/locative reflexive pronoun. Its reference follows the subject: myself, yourself, himself, herself, ourselves, themselves.

sobom.note: Instrumental reflexive pronoun; often with s/sa ('with oneself'). It can refer to any person.

tim.note: Form of taj: instrumental singular or dative/locative/instrumental plural. Separately, tim is the noun 'team'.

tih.note: Genitive plural of taj ('those'); also the masculine adjective tih ('quiet').

kom.note: Short dative/locative form used for 'whom/which'. It is not the English abbreviation 'com'.

im.note: Short dative plural personal pronoun. The stressed form is njima.

njim.note: Instrumental masculine/neuter singular pronoun. Used after prepositions, such as s njim ('with him/it').

njom.note: Instrumental feminine singular pronoun; s njom means 'with her'.

njemu.note: Stressed dative/locative masculine or neuter singular pronoun; short dative form mu.

njoj.note: Stressed dative/locative of ona. The short dative form is joj.

moga.note: Genitive masculine/neuter singular of moj, also animate masculine accusative. It is a possessive, not a form of 'can'.

kime.note: Instrumental of tko; koga is genitive/accusative and kome is dative/locative.

žele.note: Usually third-person plural present of željeti. Separately, žele is a noun meaning 'jelly'.

morala.note: Usually feminine singular past participle of morati; also genitive singular of the noun moral ('morality').

sina.note: Genitive/accusative singular of sin ('son'). The word for a rail is šina.

priči.note: Dative/locative singular of priča. Do not confuse it with prići ('to approach'), which has ć.

god.note: Indefinite particle in tko god ('whoever'), što god ('whatever'), and similar phrases. God. with a full stop abbreviates godina.

sviđa.note: Third-person singular of sviđati se. The person who likes something is dative: sviđa mi se means 'I like it'.

sviđaš.note: Second-person singular of sviđati se. Sviđaš mi se means 'I like you'; mi supplies the experiencer.

sviđam.note: First-person singular of sviđati se. In sviđam ti se, ti means 'to you': 'you like me'.

sviđaju.note: Third-person plural of sviđati se. Sviđaju mi se means 'I like them'; the liked things are the subject.

svoj.note: Reflexive possessive: one’s own, referring to the subject. Masculine singular; agrees with the possessed noun, not the owner.

svoje.note: Inflected form of svoj: neuter singular or feminine/masculine plural forms. Refers to the subject’s own possession.

svoju.note: Accusative feminine singular of svoj (one’s own), agreeing with the possessed noun; refers back to the subject.

svojim.note: Instrumental masculine/neuter singular or dative/locative/instrumental plural of svoj; the owner is the subject.

svog.note: Short genitive masculine/neuter singular, or animate masculine accusative singular, of svoj (one’s own).

svom.note: Dative/locative masculine/neuter singular or instrumental feminine singular of svoj; possession refers to the subject.

svojoj.note: Dative/locative feminine singular of svoj (one’s own), agreeing with the possessed noun.

svojih.note: Genitive plural of svoj, all genders. Means one’s own, with the owner determined by the subject.

svojom.note: Instrumental feminine singular of svoj (one’s own); the subject determines whose possession it is.

svoja.note: Feminine singular or neuter plural of svoj (one’s own), agreeing with the possessed noun.

svoga.note: Long genitive masculine/neuter singular, or animate masculine accusative singular, of svoj (one’s own).

svome.note: Dative/locative masculine/neuter singular of svoj (one’s own); the possessor is the subject.

svojem.note: Dative/locative masculine/neuter singular of svoj (one’s own), an alternative to svom/svome.

svojeg.note: Genitive masculine/neuter singular, or animate masculine accusative singular, of svoj (one’s own).

čula.note: Feminine singular past participle of čuti; also nominative/accusative plural of čulo ('sense').

ču.note: Literary aorist of čuti, second-/third-person singular. The future auxiliary 'I will' is ću, with a different letter.

sto.note: The number 100. Što ('what') is a different word and must keep its diacritic.

nađe.note: Third-person singular present of naći; also second-/third-person singular aorist. Tense depends on context.

ubit.note: Shortened infinitive of ubiti, used before a future auxiliary: ubit ću. It is not itself a past-tense form.

paru.note: Dative/locative of par ('pair/couple'); also accusative of para ('steam').

budi.note: Usually singular imperative of biti ('be!'); also a present/imperative form of buditi ('wake').

budite.note: Plural/polite imperative of biti ('be!'); also a present/imperative form of buditi ('wake').

budimo.note: First-person plural imperative of biti; also a present/imperative form of buditi ('wake').

vise.note: Third-person plural present of visjeti. Više ('more') is a different word with š.

sef.note: Masculine noun for a secure box or vault. Šef ('boss') is a different word with š.

svet.note: Masculine adjective meaning 'holy/sacred'. Standard Croatian for 'world' is svijet.

tede.note: Vocative of the name Ted, used when addressing him. Names are normally capitalized: Tede.

ser.note: Croatian spelling of the British title Sir, used before a man's name; not a general translation of 'gospodin'.

gđe.note: Inflected abbreviation of gospođa, including genitive singular. 'Where' is gdje, not gđe.

uredu.note: Dative/locative singular of ured ('office'). 'OK' is written as two words: u redu.

nazvat.note: Shortened infinitive of nazvati before a future auxiliary, as in nazvat ću ('I will call').

pisati.note: Infinitive meaning 'to write'. 'To pee' is pišati, with š.

pisalo.note: Neuter singular past participle of pisati; also a noun for a writing implement.

počet.note: Shortened infinitive of početi before a future auxiliary; also a passive participle meaning 'begun'.

smiješ.note: Present of smjeti ('may/be allowed') or, with se, smijati se ('laugh'). Both can have this spelling.

smiju.note: Third-person plural of smjeti ('may') or, with se, smijati se ('laugh').

smjela.note: Feminine singular past participle of smjeti; also feminine of the adjective smio/smjel ('bold').

smjeli.note: Masculine plural past participle of smjeti; also an adjective form meaning 'bold'.

strašno.note: Adverb meaning 'terribly/awfully', or neuter adjective 'frightening'. 'Passionately' is strastveno.

riješit.note: Shortened infinitive of riješiti before a future auxiliary; not itself a past tense.

biću.note: Dative/locative singular of biće ('being/creature'). Standard Croatian 'I will be' is written bit ću.

sustav.note: Masculine noun for a system; genitive sustava, plural sustavi. It does not mean rustling.

pozvat.note: Shortened infinitive of pozvati, used before a future auxiliary: pozvat ću.

donijet.note: Shortened infinitive of donijeti before a future auxiliary: donijet ću ('I will bring').

ručku.note: Dative/locative singular of ručak ('lunch'); also accusative singular of ručka ('handle').

ručka.note: Genitive singular of ručak ('lunch'); also the nominative noun ručka ('handle').

pale.note: Feminine plural past participle of pasti, or third-person plural present of paliti. Context distinguishes the verbs.

obzira.note: Genitive singular of obzir. Bez obzira means 'regardless'; the whole phrase supplies that meaning.

pasa.note: Genitive plural of pas ('dog'). Paša ('pasture' or the title 'pasha') has š and is a different word.

sirom.note: Instrumental singular of sir. Širom ('throughout/wide open') has š and is a different word.

šef.note: Masculine noun for a boss or chief. Sef ('safe/vault') is a different word without š.

znaci.note: Nominative plural of znak. Znači ('means') has č and is a different form.

muškaraca.note: Genitive plural of muškarac. It does not mean 'tomboy'.

pošao.note: Masculine singular past participle of poći (set off), normally used with an auxiliary. Posao, without š, means job/work.

visi.note: Third-person singular present of visjeti ('hang'). Viši ('higher/taller') has š and is a different word.

leta.note: Genitive singular of let ('flight'). Standard Croatian 'of summer' is ljeta.

pol.note: Noun 'pole', or a short form of pola ('half') in quantities. The standard word for gender/sex is spol.

guzici.note: Dative/locative singular of guzica. Vulgar/informal register; not a plural form.

love.note: Third-person plural of loviti; also genitive singular of lova ('money', slang).

čista.note: Feminine form of čist. Cista ('cyst') is a different word without č.

los.note: Masculine noun for the animal. Loš ('bad') has š and is a different word.

nek.note: Short form of neka, a particle used for third-person commands or wishes. It does not mean 'some'.

posto.note: Used after numbers for percentages. Pošto ('since/after/how much') has š and is a different word.

ted.note: Personal name, normally capitalized. The standard Croatian word for 'week' is tjedan.

kužim.note: Informal first-person singular of kužiti ('understand/get it'); it does not mean 'I am at home'.

kužiš.note: Informal second-person singular of kužiti ('understand/get it').

rijeci.note: Dative/locative singular of rijeka. Riječi ('words/of a word') has č and is a different form.

želje.note: Form of želja ('wish/desire'). Zelje ('greens/cabbage') starts with z and is a different word.

jamie.note: Personal name, normally capitalized. It is not a Croatian word for 'pits'.

gade.note: Vocative of gad (an insult), or third-person plural of gaditi (se) ('disgust'). Context distinguishes them.

lovu.note: Accusative of lov ('hunt'), or of lova ('money', slang). It is not a first-person verb form.

lova.note: Slang noun for money; also genitive singular of lov ('hunt').

gori.note: Present third-person singular of gorjeti, or a masculine comparative adjective meaning 'worse'.

kompa.note: Colloquial word for a friend; also genitive of komp, a colloquial abbreviation for 'computer'.

čas.note: Usually a moment or short time; 'hour' is literary/regional. The everyday Croatian word for an hour is sat.

kurvin.note: Possessive adjective from kurva. Vulgar, especially in insults; it is not the noun 'whore'.

carter.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

osjetila.note: Feminine singular past participle of osjetiti (feel/sense); also genitive singular or plural forms of osjetilo (sense organ).

jo.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

agente.note: Vocative singular of agent when addressing one agent; also accusative plural.

uči.note: Third-person singular present or singular imperative of učiti (learn/teach). Enter is ući, with ć.

br.note: Abbreviation br. for broj (number), normally written with a full stop.

doc.note: Abbreviation doc. for docent, an academic rank; also the nickname Doc. The full stop is normally written in the abbreviation.

liz.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

jay.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

rimu.note: Dative/locative singular of Rim (Rome), or accusative singular of rima (rhyme); capitals normally distinguish the name.

kučkin.note: Possessive adjective from kučka (bitch); insulting when applied to people.

bruce.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

jess.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

angela.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

liči.note: Present third-person singular of ličiti (paint/whitewash). For resemblance, standard Croatian uses sličiti.

minut.note: Shortened infinitive of minuti (pass/elapse), used before the future auxiliary: minut će. The noun minute is minuta.

štogod.note: Indefinite pronoun meaning something. Written separately, što god means whatever.

sad-a.note: Genitive of the abbreviation SAD (United States), normally written SAD-a. It is unrelated to sad (now).

sad-u.note: Dative/locative of SAD (United States), normally written SAD-u. It is unrelated to sad (now).

kuca.note: Present third-person singular of kucati: knocks or beats. House is kuća, with ć.

bille.note: Vocative of the personal name Bill, used when addressing him. It is not a form of biti.

miloga.note: Genitive masculine/neuter singular, or animate masculine accusative singular, of mio (dear/kind). Also in Boga miloga.

rosie.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

ethan.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

ministre.note: Vocative singular of ministar when addressing one minister; also accusative plural.

daisy.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

desetak.note: Approximate numeral noun meaning about ten, not a dozen (twelve). Following nouns normally take genitive plural.

sv.note: Abbreviation sv. for sveti (Saint); normally followed by a full stop and a name.

pam.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

brad.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

ll.note: Initials in the stage name LL Cool J; normally written uppercase. Not the Croatian word li or ili.

stone.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

bros.note: English abbreviation Bros. for brothers, used in names such as Warner Bros.; normally capitalised with a full stop.

wille.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

baker.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

smješka.note: Third-person singular present of smješkati se (smile). The reflexive se normally accompanies it.

stark.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

koliki.note: Inflected form of kolik, asking about size or quantity. It does not mean colic.

kolika.note: Feminine singular of kolik, asking how big or how much. It does not mean colic.

spavaću.note: Accusative feminine singular of spavaći, as in spavaću sobu (bedroom). I will sleep is written spavat ću.

šuma.note: Nominative singular šuma (forest); also genitive singular of šum (noise). Sum in arithmetic is suma.

ned.note: Personal name Ned, or the abbreviation ned. for nedjelja (Sunday). The abbreviation normally has a full stop.

daću.note: Accusative singular of daća (levy/tax). The future I will give is written dat ću, as two words.

toni.note: Personal name Toni; also the singular imperative of tonuti (sink). Tonnes is tone, not toni.

visočanstvo.note: Neuter noun used in royal address: Vaše Visočanstvo (Your Highness). Majesty is veličanstvo.

meri.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

reid.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

moore.note: Surname Moore, normally capitalised. It is not the Croatian common noun for a moor.

rudy.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

belle.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

marco.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

gubicu.note: Accusative singular of gubica (an animal’s muzzle); rude when used for a person’s mouth.

majk.note: Phonetic spelling of the personal name Mike. It is not a form of majka (mother).

bome.note: Emphatic particle meaning indeed/really, often expressing surprise or insistence.

lester.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

zbilo.note: Neuter singular past participle of zbiti se (happen/occur), normally used with an auxiliary and reflexive se.

bree.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

gabe.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

bik.note: Masculine noun for a bull; also the zodiac sign Taurus, normally capitalised.

isaac.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

usrani.note: Inflected passive participle/adjective from usrati; vulgar, literally soiled with excrement, often an insult.

mimi.note: Personal name or surname, normally capitalised. Retained in lowercase for case-insensitive matching.

kara.note: Personal name Kara in the intended use. Also a present form of karati; it does not mean ticket (karta).

ponovo.note: Standard adverb meaning again; ponovno is another standard form.

kaži.note: Singular imperative of kazati (say/tell). A valid standard Croatian form; reci is another common choice.

sliči.note: Present third-person singular of sličiti (resemble), used with dative: sliči majci. Ličiti means paint/whitewash.

tame.note: Genitive singular of tama (darkness). Locative singular is tami.

tjednu.note: Dative/locative singular of tjedan (week). Accusative singular is tjedan.

sati.note: Genitive plural or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of sat (hour). Genitive singular is sata.

tajni.note: Dative/locative singular or genitive plural of tajna (secret); also an adjective form of tajni (secret).

detektive.note: Vocative singular of detektiv when addressing one detective; also accusative plural.

damo.note: Vocative singular of dama (lady), used when addressing her. Also first-person plural present of dati (give).

planetu.note: Dative/locative singular of masculine planet. Also accusative singular of feminine planeta; planet is preferred in Croatian.

planete.note: Accusative plural or vocative singular of planet. Also an inflected form of feminine planeta; planet is preferred in Croatian.

liste.note: Genitive singular or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of lista (list). Also vocative singular of list (leaf/sheet).

susjede.note: Vocative singular or accusative plural of susjed (male neighbour); also inflected forms of susjeda (female neighbour).

milijardi.note: Genitive plural or dative/locative singular of milijarda (billion). Genitive singular is milijarde.

kući.note: Dative/locative singular of kuća. Idem kući means I am going home; kod kuće means at home.

mojeg.note: Genitive masculine/neuter singular of moj; also accusative masculine singular with animate nouns. Not dative.

njegove.note: Feminine genitive singular or feminine/masculine accusative plural of njegov (his); also feminine nominative plural.

njega.note: Full genitive/accusative form of on/ono (him/it), used after prepositions or for emphasis. Short form: ga.

njih.note: Full genitive/accusative plural pronoun (them), used after prepositions or for emphasis. Short form: ih.

njima.note: Dative/locative/instrumental plural pronoun: to/about/with them. Short dative: im.

nama.note: Dative/locative/instrumental of mi (we): to/about/with us. Short dative: nam.

vama.note: Dative/locative/instrumental plural or polite singular: to/about/with you. Short dative: vam.

molimo.note: First-person plural present of moliti (ask/beg), commonly a polite please; the same spelling can also be an imperative.

itko.note: Indefinite pronoun anyone/anybody, especially in questions and conditional clauses. Negative clauses normally use nitko.

gospode.note: Vocative singular of Gospod (Lord); also genitive of gospoda (gentlemen). Addressing gentlemen uses gospodo.

visosti.note: Genitive/dative/locative singular of visost (Highness); also used in the address Vaša Visosti (Your Highness).

jime.note: Vocative of the personal name Jim, used when addressing him. It is not a pronoun meaning with him.

bud.note: Personal name Bud, normally capitalised. Awake is budan.

sidney.note: Personal name Sidney, normally capitalised. The Australian city is Sydney.

kuce.note: Inflected form of kuca, a child’s word for dog. House forms use ć: kuća, kuće.

por.note: Abbreviation por. for poručnik (lieutenant), normally written with a full stop.

adama.note: Genitive/accusative singular of the personal name Adam, normally capitalised.

adame.note: Vocative of Adam, used when addressing him; normally capitalised.

braco.note: Affectionate term for a brother or a young boy; also the personal name Braco.

gad.note: Masculine noun for a nasty or contemptible person; an insult.

gadovi.note: Nominative/vocative plural of gad, an insulting term for nasty people.

glupane.note: Vocative singular of glupan (fool/idiot), used as an insult.

gđa.note: Abbreviation of gospođa (Mrs/Ms); written without a full stop.

gđo.note: Vocative singular abbreviation of gospođa, used in direct address.

gđica.note: Abbreviation of gospođica (Miss); written without a full stop.

gđice.note: Genitive or vocative singular, or nominative/accusative/vocative plural, abbreviated from gospođica.

gospo.note: Vocative singular of gospa (lady); also used to address the Virgin Mary, normally capitalised in that use.

jebiga.note: Vulgar interjection expressing resignation: fuck it/oh well. Not suitable for polite situations.

jebote.note: Vulgar exclamation expressing surprise or frustration. Its force depends on context; avoid in polite situations.

maca.note: Affectionate noun for a cat/kitty; can also have a vulgar sexual meaning. Context matters.

murjak.note: Informal, sometimes disparaging masculine noun for a police officer: cop.

kita.note: Genitive/accusative singular of kit (whale); also a feminine noun for a bunch/tuft, with a vulgar anatomical meaning.

sereš.note: Second-person singular present of srati (shit); vulgar. Often figuratively: you are talking rubbish.

šupčino.note: Vocative singular of šupčina, an emphatic vulgar insult derived from šupak.

sjeban.note: Masculine singular passive participle/adjective from sjebati; vulgar: ruined or messed up.

sjebano.note: Neuter singular passive participle/adjective from sjebati, also used adverbially; vulgar.

sjebao.note: Masculine singular past participle of sjebati, normally used with an auxiliary; vulgar.

strijelac.note: Masculine noun for an archer, shooter or goalscorer; also Sagittarius, normally capitalised as a zodiac sign.

poljubac.note: Masculine noun; genitive singular poljupca, plural poljupci. Note the changing stem.

nažalost.note: Adverb meaning unfortunately, written as one word. Na žalost is separate when žalost is a noun with a complement.

neki.note: Indefinite determiner: some/a certain. Masculine singular and masculine plural can share this spelling.

svjesna.note: Feminine singular of svjestan (aware/conscious); also neuter plural forms.

sljedećih.note: Genitive plural of sljedeći (next), all genders. Slijedeći, with ije, means while following.

budem.note: First-person singular perfective present of biti. With a past participle, forms future perfect: budem radio.

budeš.note: Second-person singular perfective present of biti; with a past participle, forms future perfect.

bude.note: Third-person singular perfective present of biti; also used in subordinate clauses and wishes.

budemo.note: First-person plural perfective present of biti; with a past participle, forms future perfect.

budete.note: Second-person plural perfective present of biti; also polite singular. With a participle, forms future perfect.

budu.note: Third-person plural perfective present of biti; with a past participle, forms future perfect.

ćete.note: Second-person plural short future auxiliary of htjeti; also polite singular. Can precede or follow the infinitive.

reklo.note: Neuter singular past participle of reći; normally used with an auxiliary. Passive said is rečeno.

rekli.note: Masculine or mixed-gender plural past participle of reći; normally used with an auxiliary.

bili.note: Masculine or mixed-gender plural past participle of biti; normally used with an auxiliary.

viđati.note: Imperfective infinitive: see repeatedly or regularly. The infinitive itself does not specify past time.

pomogne.note: Third-person singular present of perfective pomoći. Often refers to a possible or future event in a subordinate clause.

pomognete.note: Second-person plural present of perfective pomoći; also polite singular. The clause determines its time reference.

poznam.note: First-person singular present of poznati (know/be acquainted with). Poznajem is from poznavati.

pravu.note: Accusative feminine singular of prav/pravi, or dative/locative singular of pravo. U pravu si means you are right.

prijatelja.note: Genitive singular or plural, or accusative singular, of prijatelj (friend). Accusative plural is prijatelje.

tate.note: Genitive singular or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of tata (Dad). Vocative singular is tata.

sama.note: Feminine singular or neuter plural of sam (alone); also used for emphasis: herself/themselves, depending on the noun.

same.note: Feminine genitive singular or feminine/masculine accusative plural of sam; also feminine nominative plural.

nečeg.note: Short genitive form of nešto (something); nečega is the longer standard form.

nečem.note: Short dative/locative form of nešto (something); nečemu is the longer standard form.

ničeg.note: Short genitive form of ništa (nothing); ničega is the longer standard form.

nikad.note: Standard short form of nikada (never). Usually used with a negated verb.

tad.note: Standard short form of tada (then/at that time).

ono.note: Neuter singular demonstrative that (over there); also the neuter subject pronoun it.

ondje.note: Adverb for there, a location away from the speaker. Onamo indicates movement towards there.

au.note: Interjection expressing pain, surprise or alarm: ow!/oh!

dvije.note: Feminine nominative/accusative of dva (two). Following nouns normally use the counting form: dvije žene.

dečki.note: Informal nominative/vocative plural of dečko (boy/boyfriend); also dečki as an affectionate address.

provesti.note: Perfective infinitive: spend (time), conduct or carry out. The object determines the meaning.

provela.note: Feminine singular past participle of provesti: spent (time), conducted or carried out. Used with an auxiliary.

proveo.note: Masculine singular past participle of provesti: spent (time), conducted or carried out. Used with an auxiliary.

proveli.note: Masculine or mixed-gender plural past participle of provesti; used with an auxiliary.

udati.note: Perfective infinitive. Udati se means get married (of a woman); udati koga means marry someone off.

oženiti.note: Perfective infinitive. Oženiti se means get married (of a man); oženiti koga means marry someone off.

pokušajmo.note: First-person plural imperative of pokušati: let us try. Present indicative is pokušamo.

nađimo.note: First-person plural imperative of naći: let us find. Present indicative is nađemo.

uzmimo.note: First-person plural imperative of uzeti: let us take. Present indicative is uzmemo.

božić.note: Masculine noun for Christmas, normally written Božić. Genitive singular is Božića.

cimer.note: Masculine noun meaning roommate; conversational Croatian. Feminine counterpart: cimerica.

negoli.note: Conjunction meaning than, especially after a comparative. Negoli is a longer form of nego.

marie.note: Personal name Marie, or an inflected form of Maria; normally capitalised. It does not mean the verb marry.

franka.note: Genitive singular of franak (franc), or the personal name Franka; normally capitalised when a name.

aha.note: Interjection expressing recognition or understanding: aha!/I see!

obećam.note: First-person singular perfective present of obećati (promise). Imperfective counterpart: obećavam.

cijel.note: Masculine singular indefinite form of the adjective meaning whole/entire. Definite form: cijeli.

želudac.note: Masculine noun for the stomach; genitive želuca, plural želuci. Note the changing stem.

sedmice.note: Genitive singular or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of sedmica (the number seven). Standard Croatian for weeks is tjedni.

možda.note: Adverb meaning maybe/perhaps. It expresses uncertainty, not a grammatical future tense.

jebeni.note: Masculine plural or definite masculine singular adjective from jebati; vulgar intensifier, roughly fucking/damned.

jebeno.note: Neuter singular adjective or adverb from jebati; vulgar intensifier. Its force and meaning depend on context.

jebena.note: Feminine singular or neuter plural adjective from jebati; vulgar intensifier.

jebenu.note: Accusative feminine singular adjective from jebati; vulgar intensifier.

jebene.note: Feminine genitive singular or feminine/masculine plural adjective forms from jebati; vulgar intensifier.

jebenog.note: Genitive masculine/neuter singular, or animate masculine accusative singular, of jeben; vulgar intensifier.

jebenom.note: Dative/locative masculine/neuter singular or instrumental feminine singular of jeben; vulgar intensifier.

jebenih.note: Genitive plural of jeben, all genders; vulgar intensifier.

poslušaj.note: Singular imperative of poslušati: listen! Perfective, requesting a particular act of listening.

savršeni.note: Definite masculine singular or masculine plural forms of savršen (perfect). Agreement depends on the noun.

mačku.note: Accusative singular of mačka (female cat); also dative/locative singular of mačak (male cat).

posljednju.note: Accusative feminine singular of posljednji (last), agreeing with a feminine direct object.

navikao.note: Masculine singular past participle of navići. With se, means became accustomed; auxiliary supplies person and tense.

isprva.note: Adverb meaning at first/initially; written as one word.

naoružan.note: Masculine singular passive participle/adjective of naoružati (arm/equip with weapons).

petera.note: Genitive/accusative singular of the personal name Peter, normally capitalised.

odemo.note: First-person plural present of otići (leave/go away). A perfective present; time reference depends on the clause.

sretno.note: Adverb meaning happily/with good fortune; also the wish good luck! Neuter adjective forms can share the spelling.

govno.note: Vulgar neuter noun for excrement; also an insult.

govna.note: Genitive singular or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of govno; vulgar.

guzica.note: Feminine noun for buttocks/arse; rude or very informal.

guzice.note: Genitive singular or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of guzica; rude/informal.

jebati.note: Imperfective infinitive; vulgar verb meaning fuck, often used in curses.

jebao.note: Masculine singular past participle of jebati, normally used with an auxiliary; vulgar.

jebe.note: Third-person singular present of jebati; vulgar, often used in curses or expressions of indifference.

jebem.note: First-person singular present of jebati; vulgar, often used in curses.

jebeš.note: Second-person singular present of jebati; vulgar, also used in dismissive expressions.

jebi.note: Second-person singular imperative of jebati; vulgar.

kopile.note: Neuter noun for a child born outside marriage, now chiefly an insulting term; offensive.

kuja.note: Feminine noun for a female dog; offensive when applied to a woman.

kujo.note: Vocative singular of kuja; an offensive insult when addressed to a woman.

kučka.note: Feminine noun for a female dog; offensive when applied to a woman.

kučko.note: Vocative singular of kučka; an offensive insult when addressed to a woman.

kurac.note: Vulgar masculine noun for penis, also used in curses and dismissive expressions.

kurve.note: Genitive singular or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of kurva; derogatory/vulgar.

kurvo.note: Vocative singular of kurva; an offensive insult.

muda.note: Nominative/accusative/vocative plural of mudo (testicle); vulgar, also figurative for courage.

odjebi.note: Singular imperative of odjebati, a vulgar command meaning fuck off.

seronja.note: Masculine noun following feminine-type declension; vulgar insult for an obnoxious person.

seronje.note: Genitive singular or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of seronja; vulgar insult.

seronjo.note: Vocative singular of seronja; vulgar insult.

sranje.note: Vulgar neuter noun: shit, a mess or rubbish, depending on context.

sranja.note: Genitive singular or nominative/accusative/vocative plural of sranje; vulgar.

šupak.note: Vulgar masculine noun, literally anus; often an insult for an unpleasant person.

zajebao.note: Masculine singular past participle of zajebati (mess up/trick); vulgar.

zajebavati.note: Imperfective infinitive: tease, mess with or fool someone; vulgar. With se, can mean joke around.

zajebi.note: Singular imperative of zajebati; vulgar, often used to dismiss something: forget it/screw it.

stražnjica.note: Feminine noun for the buttocks/bottom; a neutral alternative to vulgar anatomical terms.

kupaonica.note: Feminine noun for a bathroom; genitive singular kupaonice, locative singular kupaonici.

đavao.note: Masculine noun for a devil; genitive singular đavla. Note the changing stem.

obveza.note: Feminine noun for an obligation or duty; genitive singular obveze.

partner.note: Masculine noun for a partner, whether in a relationship or a shared activity. Feminine counterpart: partnerica.

nećaka.note: Genitive/accusative singular of nećak (nephew); also the feminine noun nećaka (niece). Nećakinja is the usual Croatian feminine form.

review_method: All 3,768 original translation families reviewed; explanation templates reviewed and inflection claims cross-checked with hrLex; individual exceptions hand-edited. Not a native-speaker certification.
